I have since purchased 4 more lol and each time set up has been great no buffering. No internet issues. It's been great and I hope to be able to save so much money using the amazon Firestick! If you're on the fence do it! It's awesome  Edit 8/28/2019:  After playing with this and streaming TV through the app I realized it's sucking way more data than I had previously thought. Don't get me wrong the streaming service is awesome and the apps work great! Loved it but in our household it's not going to work. Unlimited data with Comcast would be $100 and unlimited by itself with direct TV will be $90. My satellite direct TV with unlimited internet not that much more expensive. I ran the device the morning for several hours and figured it's using 6.6gb an hour. I even changed the resolution to 720p and I'm shocked it is using that much data. My parents are retired and literally have the TV on for like 17 hours a day. I calculated how much how much data we would use and it would be like 3TB a month. That's insane.  That being said I will keep these because I love the features and with used sparingly it won't be an issue. When storms come through and knock out the satellite it will be a great backup device as well, I still think it's worth buying even if you keep your cable service.  Edit #2, So I checked our data and the boxes had not been being used and we were at 35gb for the day. I was confused because they had not been on. So the next day I unplugged the firesticks and low and behold our internet usage was cut in half. The firesticks continue to use data and STAY ON even when you think you have turned them off. So if you are concerned about Data usage simply unplug the device when not in use and when you use it plug it back in. No big deal. It powered right up for me and all my settings were saved. We may at some point down the line still cancel our cable and go with unlimited internet but I can't make up my mind. I absolutely love the firestick and use it in the kitchen and bedrooms. The Amazon prime exercise videos my mom loves. So its still a win-win. Just needed to keep them off when not in use to save on data.  Edit/ Update #3-- I finally cut the cord 6 months ago. We no longer have to unplug the devices whatever was sucking data seems to have resolved itself. We just make sure to go back to the home screen (exit any applications) and then turn it off when not in use. We use Pluto (free) Philo $20 and FrndlyTV $5.99. the reason we completely cut the cord is because DirecTV decided to raise our bill to $190 a month. My internet bill alone is $70 so even after friendly I'm still saving $80 a month by cutting the cord. Our internet usage typically doesn't even get to 300gb for the month the resolution set to 720p. I have 5 firesticks now lol one in each room. I don't see a need to ever have cable again. ;)

I'm a Prime member but rarely used the video&music portion of my membership. Previously I was accessing the video thru my DVD player which had a clunky user interface (which is probably why I didn't use it much). Amazon ended support of the Sony products. I got a $25 discount code and thought...why not. I have an older 1080 HDTV but opted for the 4K FireTV to be prepared for a future TV upgrade, plus cashed in some of my Amazon Rewards and had this for free. Biggest complaint is the remote, specifically, the back is a real PITA to get open. I have literally opened thousands of battery compartments. Nearly every one in intuitive. I expected this to be the same, but NOOO, I struggled with it for a good 15min before finally heading to google for some assistance. It seems that this is by far and away the biggest complaint. Do yourself a favor, don't struggle with the remote like I did, head over to google or youtube and watch a video or two and you will get it open fairly quickly. Amazon needs to change the design of the remote battery cover and/or get the quick start/manual updated, because it is clearly not as simple as "open the remote and install the batteries"...but in all honesty, opening the battery compartment is something that will be done infrequently and you really don't want to cover popping open every time the remote drops on the floor (which already happened a few times for me). Other than the hassle with the remote battery cover, I had this up and connected to my wifi with 10min. After the connection was established the FireTV automatically updated and rebooted. This took several more minutes but in no time I was clicking thru the many video and music choices. There are quite a few settings in various menus. One thing I don't like is that the whole Alexia. Maybe I'm a bit of a foil-hat but I have not bought into the whole auto-everything home. I also have a programmable remote control that I used for my entertainment center (older LogicTech 650) that works well. I don't need or want the FireTV controlling all my devices, indeed it can't because the FireTV remote does not have options for amp, tuner, DVD, CD, turntable, cable/DVR. One final irk, there is no sleep/power button for the FireTV. The power button on the remote is only for controlling external devices (i.e. TV) and my LogicTech manages all my prerprogrammed settings just fine. In order to put the FireTV to sleep, you need to press and hold the Home button to access a mini-menu where Sleep is an option. I did find the menu for Controllers and Bluetooth Devices and was able to pair an old keyboard that I used with my KindleFire. The video, music and photo services are great. Was watching video and listening to music in not time (after the initial setup, update, reboot). There are pluses and minuses to the Amazon video and music services, as I use them more I'm sure I will get them customized to my liking. For now I'll still use Pandora for music as I am more familiar with it and already have many "stations" created to suit my various moods and situational settings. Previously, with my DVD player access, I was not able to take advantage of the photos options. I uploaded some recent photos and wow, quite impressed with how they look on the TV, wife loved it. As a Prime member I have unlimited photos so this is looking like a great option and an easy way to share and view all my photos (of course it won't be my only backup, because to put all your eggs in one basket just not very smart). The keyboard made it handy to use the web apps such as Firefox and YouTube. My keyboard was a bit klunky and I'm going to pick up one with a glide pad for easier mouse/pointing. Overall very happy. The user interface is far better than with my Sony DVD and as such FireTV will get used frequently in this house.

I have to say: I'm pretty impressed with the new FireStick. I previously owned a FireTV 2nd edition, which to this day no other Fire TV seems to hold a candle to, so I have to admit I wasn't expecting much out of this device.  I've pretty much tested it into the ground at this point but I'm still no where near complete as I don't have some of the necessary features like Dolby Atmos and an HDR tv to really see what it can do. Even with that being said, I can attest that it does hit the 4k resolution as promised.  I unfortunately could not connect this directly to my receiver(a pioneer vsx 520) as it would not pick up the 4k resolution. I opted to use the ARC function available, and that at least gave me some functionality though it doesn't quite seem to work well with anything other than the regular dolby digital 5.1 format.  A few times I found it dropping the ARC connection from the TV but I honestly don't know how much of a role the stick is playing in this occurrence. I was pretty surprised how well the Wifi handles on this device. At close distances it was able to use all of my 300mbit connection down but for some reason it split the upload speed in half.  Going much further out, about 40 ft, I definitely saw a huge drop in the connection showing about 40mbit down and up which was still good enough for streaming much of my media. I own an HDHomeRun Connect OTA which ran fine after an update.  I'm a big KODI user, and though Amazon doesn't support the application, I found it pretty easy to get around this and install it using the Downloader app. This allowed me to test most of my personal media. Initially, I was having issues playing my DVD iso's but after updating KODI to 18.1 RC1, things started to work. I did, however, have to take off the hardware codec as the movies were choppy for some reason. Apparently, this has been an ongoing issue.  If your not into DVD menu's like myself, you can just use the MKV format with the mpeg-2 codec and things will run fine. I also tried a few Blu-Rays as well. The H.264 codec with the MP4 format worked without a problem but using the MKV format with the VC1 had stuttering issues.  If you have a good media server, than I just recommend transcoding with Plex or Emby as converting can take forever. The device did a great job with switching resolutions and frame rates for 24fps mode so if you have a TV that has these functions available, breath easy.  Lastly I tested out some games. The FireStick unfortunately only supports three controllers at this time the Xbox One, PlayStation 4(ver 2), and the Matricom(I specifically used G-PAD BX). I grabbed RetroArch, a great multi emulation application.  It would seem the PlayStation is far as you are going to get for good performance on 3D accelerated games. I tried out the Run-Ahead feature for latency reduction on some of the older titles and it worked pretty well baring a few issues with certain games. I do believe that some N64 and PSP games can work with the FireStick but it is recommend you use the separate emulators rather than RetroArch to run them.  I'm no where near done with trying things out but as you can see, the FireStick 4K does hold up pretty well for the price. The interface is snappy and integration seems to be pretty painless so if you're looking for a budget media player you can use for the mean time or for a secondary room this is definitely the one I recommend.

The device comes with 5gb of available storage and a few unnecessary apps already installed. After installing a few 5-6 apps depending on the size you will be having to delete some files due to the limited space. Some apps also download adds to the stick so it really can be filled easily.  The only available remedy for this is to use an otg cable to add a useable USB port for expansion via a thumb drive and use third party software. Either the cable should come included with purchase or the device should be redesigned to include a micro sd slot and proper software support integrated to move apps and data.  By default the stick doesn’t work with any of my game controllers besides a ps5 controller and using that the button mappings are out of wack and a few essential buttons are just not usable, the main being rb and the O button are entirely non functional and can’t be mapped using any software even third party. Steam controllers and switch controllers do not work with the stick, you can pair but they’re not useable. And this is across all fire tv devices.  I wish they released a new stick with 6gb of ram, 32gb of internal storage and an expansion micro sd slot or to include the otg cable rather than the max they just released which is a minimal upgrade from this one. If anyone from Amazon actually reads these reviews please know that I would be willing to spend up to 75 dollars for a stick with the above included as it would remedy most of my issues with the device, if they could do both the slot and include the otg cable it would be the best of both worlds for any normal user who doesn’t want to mess around with third party software.  Currently I use this stick in a Christie lwu510i projector and it’s been working great minus the above issues. The stick can be powered by the projectors onboard usb rather than using an external source as long as the micro usb cable that Is used to power the stick is under 6 inches in length, then enough power comes out to fully use the stick and you will get no warning messages. I have the audio coming from the sticks Bluetooth into a echo dot that has its aux cord plugged into an old avr for full 7.1 support, it has some delay issues intermittently but it can be resolved by disconnecting and reconnecting or messing around with the av sync options but the sync options seem to be hit or miss and sometimes doesn’t even apply changes made in it.  Using the ps5 controller and GeForce now I have been able to play a few games thanks to being able to remap some buttons but it’s still not a optimal experience, maybe a cheap controller would work better but unfortunately if you have a bunch of controllers already from other consoles they probably will have issues, I would recommend either the Luna controller or a cheap android based one as this would most likely solve the mapping issues since it doesn’t seem like Amazon will be doing anything to help make the other controllers function.  And now finally the reason I say the stick needs more ram, while using the web browser to watch anything if the browser page has an abundance of adds it will cause the stick to overflow and the video your watching will start to stutter until you refresh the page to clear the cache only for it to occur again once enough ads have loaded, if they included both the onboard storage extensions and more ram this will remedy this issue. It would also make some browser games playable which would be a huge bonus going forward since game streaming seems to be the future focus.  Also if it’s possible I would suggest someone to include the ability to talk to any other Alexa device and have it still able to use the controllers ir blaster to turn devices on and off, as it stands now if I talk to my phone or my echo devices it can’t turn the projector or my avr on or off while only the remote can, I would love if you could have it still use the ir from the remote to control devices while talking to those other echo devices or using the app on your phone.

I had a Fire Stick on my tv in the guest room rather than a cable box, and the grandkids mostly used it. Frustrated with my cable provider cost and service, I moved that Fire Stick to my main tv to try out for a couple of weeks. I was very happy with the content, ease of use, etc. so I purchased this Fire Stick for my main tv, upped my internet service speed (had a few instances of buffering and freeze on my old, very basic, very slow internet service), and I canceled my cable tv service. My monthly bill was cut in half, so in 1 month I recouped more than the device cost.  As an Amazon Prime member, I get a lot great Prime original content and have access to many other shows and movies at no extra charge. I'm still learning all of the features and capabilities of this device. The voice command button, our gal pal Alexa, is extremely helpful with this and with finding shows and content. I really appreciate the remote's pause feature which provides the names of actors in the scene I'm watching, especially in older shows with actors who look familiar, but whose name I don't recall. I can pause what I'm watching at any time, go to other content, and come back to what I was watching when I want. If I miss something while watching, via the voice command button on the remote, I can ask to rewind any number of seconds, minutes or even restart the content from the beginning. I can resume watching content from where I left it even days later.  I'll likely purchase a compact antenna to allow me to view local broadcast stations/news, but even without subscribing to for-pay streaming services, I'm finding plenty of content that interests me: Prime content, movies, old tv shows, national news (delayed), etc. If you're able to surf the net on a computer and are willing to take a little time to browse thru and play with the features and capabilities, I'd definitely recommend you get a Fire Stick.  If you're not comfortable working on a computer or using a web browser or smart phone, you might find using the Fire Stick a little confusing. My 86 year-old mom can access FB on her Fire tablet and would really enjoy access to some of the content available via the Fire Stick, but I won't suggest that she buy one as it would likely be too confusing and end up frustrating her. My 6 and 8 year-old grandkids, however, whiz thru using the Fire Stick and access YouTube, games, tv shows, etc. have since day 1. They've been using Fire tablets since they were toddlers, so navigating its menu system is natural to them, even for one that cannot yet read. I also was able to set up parental controls on the Fire Sticks so that the kids cannot access inappropriate teen and above-rated content accidentally.  I'm sure there is more for me to learn about the Fire Stick; learned a couple of days ago that I can send content that I'm streaming on my Echo Show to both Fire Sticks and view/hear it on those tvs simultaneously. There's an option that allowed me to sync the audio between the devices.  I would definitely recommend this product to anyone looking to cut their cable, access all kinds of content with ease and take control of what they want to watch, when they want to watch it.

So you’ve heard about cutting the cord and you’re excited to save a little money, or you remember when you could stream just about any movie on Netflix, and you think a Fire TV Stick is the answer. The Amazon Fire TV Stick isn’t very expensive, but if you don’t wish to deal with the stress or disappointment, do your research first. After getting sick of paying for a whole cable subscription to watch nothing but local news, I installed a $600 antenna, only to find out the only channels available over the air in my area are PBS. After hearing about the Fire TV Stick, I thought I had found the answer. I was wrong. NOTHING on the Firestick is free. You will still have to create accounts through secondary companies. Most require a subscription which also risks identity and personal security. Based upon my significant other’s three favorite shows and my three favorite shows, the fees and subscriptions would pay our cable bill, and we’re unable to view everything on Firestick that we can with our basic cable subscription. Even worse, all the Fire TV Stick does is function as a hardware device which combines your choice of apps for viewing on a television. All my phones and all my laptops do that with most of my televisions already. The Fire TV Stick doesn’t magically let you watch anything for free. It’s Christmas time and we want to watch Christmas Vacation. Even with a Netflix subscription, I’m still expected to pay a rental fee. I thought I could find it and stream it for free, somewhere. Nope. The Fire Stick must have it somewhere. Nope. I finally got mad and jail broke my Firestick and installed Kodi. Still no! I can find it and I can stream it, but I still must pay a rental fee. This was the final straw and my Firestick just moved to its final resting place in the dumpster. If not being able to cut the cord and watch similar programming for free isn’t an issue, there’s more. You want to watch a specific movie or TV program? There’s no search function. Select your category or genre and click, click, click………..it’s been thirty minutes and I still haven’t found Christmas Vacation, AND IT’S CHRISTMAS TIME!!! Local TV? Not on Firestick! Local broadcasts and over the air TV are necessary to aid in keeping the population informed. If you cut the cord and rely on Firestick for entertainment, you and the rest of the Firestick population will certainly be so uninformed that certain politicians may or may not make it into office. Yet, at least you’ll be shielded from the stress of the campaign. Forest fires are heading in your direction and it’s time to evacuate. You won’t have local programming so at least you won’t have to pack your belongings since you don’t know your house will burn down. Amazon needs to realize what laws now apply to them and they need to make local programming and over the air broadcasts available on the Fire TV Stick FOR FREE! That’s why it’s free. Amazon’s technology has exceeded current systems which identifies a change in infrastructure. If the Firestick is reaching a broader population, Amazons structure must change as well. Enjoy watching a specific TV show? If you find it and pay to watch it, you must select it by the season and episode. For a device which is marketed for its ease of use, there are excessive steps necessary just to view the latest episode of your favorite show. I downloaded other apps and even when using the search bar in the apps, if I try to use the voice control it reverts to the Firestick and not the app I’m using. It will kick me out and take me back to the home screen with basically a Netflix search, nothing else. It’s not easy to use, as marketed. Even worse, I heard I had to install Kodi to make it work the way I want. I did and as I previously explained, everything still requires a subscription. I’m not done yet, I didn’t realize what I was doing is called “jail breaking” and now I’m at risk of my IP address being tracked and if I’m caught illegally viewing TV or movies, I will lose my internet service and I can be liable for royalties and fees. I can’t risk losing what I’ve worked so hard to gain, hence why my Firestick went in the trash can. If you think you can cut the cord and view TV or movies for free, you will be taking a legal risk of liability. This is actually my second review. After my first review an Amazon representative called me and asked what and why and all kinds of other questions; not interested in my true opinion, but simply to argue with me over the valid points I was making. In the end, when I explained my problem is not with Amazon, my complaint is that the Firestick does not operate as I expected it to, based upon the marketing and advertising intended to deceive the public. The Firestick functions as Amazon intends it to, but the deception Amazon has created is where my disappointment stems. The Amazon representative deleted my review…yet another deception. The Amazon Fire TV Stick is a big deception, disappointment, and legal liability.

Bought back in 2018 and still working as good as new to stream my apps. Would recommend it if you don't own your own smart TV or just want something portable for your streaming apps. One thing I wish I could use it on a laptop. Not sure if it's possible, but I haven't figured it out yet.

I recently ordered this fire TV stick in combination with a couple echo dots to dip my toes in the water, and see how I enjoyed the "Alexa experience." I'm very pleased! A little backstory--we have a smart TV, though it's not very "smart." It just doesn't offer all the apps we want, so I have always used a ROKU device with it. Sadly, I recently broke our ROKU out of sheer clumsiness. I was about to order a new one, but my kids had asked for Alexa for Christmas, so I took a moment to do some research on the array of gadgets that Amazon offers. The fire TV stick and echo dots (on special 2/$50 at the time) were a relatively low risk initial investment before possibly purchasing more devices.  First off, the voice feature included on the TV remote works well and accurately. You simply press the microphone button, pause for half a second while the feature activates and then tell it what you want to watch. I took this a step further, however, and connected my fire TV stick with one of my echo dots. That way I can tell Alexa what I want completely hands-free. I just have to specify, "on fire TV," with my command.  Another nice feature on the remote is the ability to control the TV volume and power. During setup, you're prompted to pair the remote with your TV to unlock that functionality. Another downside to our TV (gosh this TV is big, amazing and beautiful, but it's got a couple quirks, for sure) is that the remote sucks. Doesn't matter if it has fresh batteries, we're always struggling to get the TV and the remote to communicate properly. So I was pretty happy that the fire TV stick almost completely eliminates any need for the original TV remote. The only thing we ever need it for now is to change some TV specific settings. To just watch and enjoy, only the fire remote is necessary.  As far as the offerings available on Fire TV, the list is endless. It's what you've come to expect from just about any similar device, I think. All major providers such as Netflix, Hulu, Sling TV, etc., along with all major network apps like CBS, NBC, STARZ, Cinemax, HBO and so on. I couldn't even tell you everything you can get because the list is that expansive. Because it is an Amazon product and we are Prime subscribers, it plays especially nice with all of the Amazon services.  A happy discovery I made as well was that with Amazon Music (another service I subscribe to), not only do you get those handy lyrics on the phone app, but they are also on the fire TV app! Hellooooo karaoke party in my living room! If you want some better sound, the fire stick will also pair via bluetooth with an external speaker or an echo device. The smaller echo dots offer decent sound, but I do believe my next purchase will be an echo plus for something even better. Alternatively, there are also stereo configurations sold here on Amazon that play well with Alexa and fire TV.  The user interface of the fire TV stick is easy enough to navigate. It's perhaps a bit more complex than the simplicity of the ROKU I was used to, but nothing one can't manage.  All in all, I plan on purchasing more Alexa-enabled devices, in addition to another fire stick for my bedroom TV. We are really enjoying all the handy things Amazon and their great line of gadgets bring to our home.

I purchased 3 of these altogether after buying 1 and trying it out and liking it for the most part. Mostly pro's here but a few cons. I never purchased a fire stick in the past due to their limited hardware and I never was a stream freak but for years I streamed music and movies locally from pc to pc using windows smb and kodi media center for htpc client in the living room. This year I remodelled the living room completely and parted ways with the laptop, 3dtv, and 5.1 surround sound. With new walls, flooring, and new furniture I decided to get a new tv and hanging shelf and do away with anything clunky and un-used. I purchased a Samsung QLED Q9F 65" and wall mounted it above a hanging shelf and around that time I noticed as I was doing some shopping on Amazon that this new 4k fire stick had just released and it could run kodi with not much effort and handle 4k streams. My tv already had lots of online streaming apps but afaik not capable of running kodi or if possible it could I still didn't want to use a 3rd party app to download and install it on the tv memory so I chose the fire stick. All the online streaming apps run great and so does Kodi. The only con is that it doesn't have a good enough gpu and/or cpu to handle 4k remux or complete 4k bluray iso files without skipping. I had to encode to crf 17 and I think at that resolution the highest bitrate that works is 30MB/s or less. It bothers me that it is sooo close to being perfect but for the price it is totally worth it. It will play full 1080p remux and bluray img files flawlessly it's just that it wont quite do lossless 4k. It does however handle atmos 7.1 with no issues as far as I can tell and HDR as well. It also pairs well with my tv for the fact that it is almost the same remote in size and by design and for most functions it will even serve as the tv remote for almost everything. If you are bothered by the volume control on the Q9F remote then it helps to use the fire stick remote to turn the volume up or down instead of using bixby voice to do it in increments that you set. I havn't tested the wifi due to purchasing the ethernet jack but I do run a 5ghz wifi network and it should perform well due to being close to the access point but with local streaming I've always preferred wired. I'm amazed at what it does handle due to being small in size and fairly cheap in price but a future 4k fire box is in need of for anybody serious about lossless streaming. I'd say 8gb of ram/quad core intel cpu/gpu capable of rendering 4k res at full bitrate/and built in gigabit or 10gig ethernet and it should be able to monster everything around. In the meantime if you are running kodi from a pc for 3d and/or 1080p and you are looking to do 4k, then stick to pc with a 1080ti or better and lossless 4k aint a problem, but otherwise encoded 4k movies using profile main 10 with a crf of 17 will run perfect throughout the entire movie on this 4k fire stick. It is easy to setup hardware wise and during the on screen setup it's very straight forward. I'm only giving it 4 stars cause I think it should've had more ram, more memory for apps and storage considering solid state and thumb drives store so much in a small form factor these days, and gigabit should've been fit to the device directly and/or at least offered in addon adaptor. Even with a slightly higher price these perks could've put it at the top of the streaming tech race but if you don't have a fire stick at all and you have amazon prime, netflix, 4k movies of your own and time to encode them then don't hesitate to buy. It's totally worth it at it's current price.

First off, I had the previous iteration of this device, the Fire TV Pendent. It worked pretty well at the time, but with this upgrade, a major selling point for me was the remote and the faster CPU. Once I plugged the device in and fired it up and got it configured, I could definitely see a major speed increase over the Pendent (which wasn't that much of slouch to begin with).  Set up was easy, but initial will take some time as it also updates the device to the latest software. Once that is done, it will walk you through steps to integrate the remote with your TV. If it works, you'll have a remote for the Fire TV as well as your TV where you can power on and off your tv, control the volume of the TV, and if compatible with your TV, you can use the voice control to switch from one HDMI port to another as well as to your cable port if you have cable or a digital antenna, which is what I have as we dumped cable years ago.  My surround set up is a bit different. I have a DTS decoder hooked up to a set of 5.1 surround sound speakers but it only has an optical input so I have to attach the TV optical out to the decoder's optical input port. But it works. But, I have no way to control the decoder unfortunately, so I still have to have 2 remotes: 1 for the Fire TV and the other for the decoder (for volume control, etc). But, that's better than when I had to have 3 remotes. However, another draw-back is there is no way to switch channels on your TV that I have found without the use of the actual TV remote, so you'll still want to keep that handy.  But, overall, this device is a great upgrade if you have the previous incantation of the Fire TV. Picture quality is excellent and surround sound is excellent. The reason I chose this over the Roku Streaming Stick+ (which we have in our living room TV) is I found that the Plex Player app on the Fire TV device handles DTS whereas on the Roku, it doesn't. No sound whatsoever. It won't down-mix or anything even though my decoder handles DTS. This is with Direct Play turned on.  With the Fire TV device, it works just fine. Also, with the Fire TV Plex Player app, it is much more configurable. You can have it handle either optical or HDMI pass-through. Roku doesn't give you this option. And since my TV only has an optical out, that is my only option to get it hooked up to pass the DTS signal through to the decoder.  My only other gripe (and I've done all I can to fix it), is that WiFi streaming will stop after an hour or so and will require a device restart to fix it. No other devices are affected by it and the router is a Netgear Nighthawk R7000 (AC1900). It handles the correct 5ghz WiFi protocol for the Fire TV 4K stick and yet, unless I have the Fire TV stick hooked up to the LAN adapter dongle, I'll get issues where the network connection over WiFi (2.4ghz as well as 5ghz) will go out after about an hour or so. The Roku does NOT experience this issue nor any other device hooked up to the router. But, since I do a lot of watching my Blu-Ray collection on my Plex media server, I find that the Fire TV device handles every one of my movies without issue (whether it's AC3 or DTS audio). The Roku, not so much. Some movies it refuses to even stream or others no sound (whether it's through the TV or through my DTS decoder). Definitely Roku's software seems to be behind the times as it's hardware might be as well.

First of all, I own two of these, and the Fire TV AKA Firestick is a very good device. I highly recommend it overall for all the reasons that many other reviewers are singing its praises. It does many, many things very well. It gets 5 stars for voice recognition, stream quality, and Alexa integration. I love having all my content available on one home screen. Roku does a very good, job as do the other competitors to Firestick, but Amazon's device is clearly the best of the bunch, in my opinion. Though I will say that the others are getting better, too.  By the way, a lot of people complain about there being so many advertisements on the Home Screen and other content screens on the Firestick. But I disagree with this. Because it isn't like Amazon is spamming us with ads for dishwashers and outdoor BBQ's lol. They have simply created a huge landscape with tons of channels and content that in many cases I would not have even known about were it not for the ads and icons for them. To me, this is a plus not a minus. I have some minor niggles with the Alexa integration and sometimes the wonky connectivity of either the Firestick remote (in my bedroom) or the Logitech Harmony Elite I use in the living room. BUT these things, in my estimation, are part of the natural evolution of the platform, and they have been getting steadily better since I started using Firestick a few years ago. So I am being patient about this.  I love the fact that I can simply add all my cable channels that I currently subscribe to and watch them with corresponding apps. I subscribe to ALL the channels through Optimum Online, and pay the monthly subscriptions, but it is incredibly convenient to have the apps on various devices, especially the Firestick, so that the term "cutting the cord" is really true, as cliché as it sounds. But this brings me to my problem. It may not be entirely Amazon's fault, either, but Amazon has to accept some blame here, too.  The problem is that I pay my monthly fee for Cinemax, just as I do for all the HBO's, Showtime services, and pretty much everything except for the adult channels like Spice or Playboy. Yet, mysteriously there is no MaxGo or Cinemax app on the Firestick.  Now anyone in the know will likely get snippy now and say that its not Amazon's fault because Cinemax, HBO's sister channel, needs to make their app compatible with the Firestick platform, and so far they have refused. So Amazon cannot allow Firestick or Prime members to download an app that the devs on the Cinemax team have not created for the Firestick, right? True, and you would be 100% correct to point this out to me.  But hear me out first before flaming the review lol (I wish I could make that bold)  Where Amazon is dropping the ball is by offering the channel as a subscription service and placing it smack, dab in the middle of my home screen. Why is this so bad? Simple! Amazon Prime is offering a separate (completely separate) subscription to Cinemax. So, what this means to anyone who subscribes to Cinemax through our cable companies, like I do, now have two choice:  1. Pay for Cinemax twice; Once to your cable company AND then to Amazon as a premium add-on to Prime Video  2. Not have access to Cinemax on your Firestick at all, BUT you have to now be spammed by the advertisement FOR A CHANNEL YOU ARE ALREADY PAYING FOR but can't watch unless you pay again every month!  While you cannot download a nonexistent app, and I certainly do not blame Amazon or its Prime Video division for that, Amazon NEEDS to embargo this channel until Cinemax creates an app for the Firestick platform. So I am knocking off TWO full stars from my review until such time as Amazon fixes this. If they do, I will adjust my review to 4.5 Stars, rounded up to 5.  Either they need to find a way to entice Cinemax to make the app compatible with Firestick or they need to completely embargo all Cinemax content from the Firestick. At the very least, they need to STOP advertising that channel on the Home screen so that they aren't encouraging this Cinemax-developer laziness. I say laziness, because MaxGo is available as an app for the PC, iOS, and Android devices.  Why Amazon (and Apple, and Roku) tolerate this is completely beyond me. But Amazon is a hugely powerful international company. They have the power, along with Apple and Roku, to exert incredible pressure on unscrupulous (or just lazy) channel companies like Cinemax to do the right thing. They may not be able to force these devs (and I am sure Cinemax is not the only one) to make their apps compatible, but they can certainly embargo the content until they do.  So, as I said, my review will remain a firm 3 stars until Amazon either demands Cinemax fix this OR Amazon does the right thing with a embargo on the channel until they do. Although, I am aware that some people who DO NOT subscribe to Cinemax through their cable/satellite providers will object to this because they are NOT being forced to pay twice.  So my compromise is this: There should at least be a way for people like me to REMOVE all advertisements for Cinemax from my Home screen completely, even without an absolute embargo. I should NOT have to endure advertisements to PAY TWICE for a channel, but I am also well aware that it would be unfair to completely embargo the channel for people not subscribing to all the channels and who choose to pay Amazon Prime instead. They should be able to do so.

If you're upgrading from the non-4K 2nd-gen ("basic") Fire Stick, with the original remote, the first thing you'll notice is that the new remote can control the power and volume on your TV and/or AV receiver -- a massive upgrade. The second thing you'll notice is how much smoother and quicker the on-screen controls respond to the remote's commands; really, the difference is not insignificant. The 4K Fire Stick is a pleasure to use compared to the often-sluggish basic version, in almost every way.  Since I'm still using a standard 1080p HDTV and not 4K I haven't yet noticed a difference in picture quality, but the big deal here is the audio -- a double-edged sword if there ever was one, if you have a multi-channel receiver and speaker setup and use a streaming app for live TV.  The 4K Fire Stick has different audio settings than the basic Fire Stick on which, under "Audio," the sub-setting "Dolby Digital Output" can be set to (1) "Dolby Digital Plus Automatic," (2) "Dolby Digital Plus OFF," (3) "Dolby Digital Plus over HDMI" or (4) "Dolby Digital over HDMI." On the 4K Fire Stick, the sub-setting under "Audio" is "Surround Sound" which also has four settings: (1) "Best Available," (2) "Stereo," (3) "Always Dolby Digital Plus" and (4) "Always Dolby Digital." The following paragraph describes what happens with the 4K Fire Stick set to "Best Available," compared to the basic Fire Stick set to "Dolby Digital Plus Automatic," each of which is the default setting for the respective devices:  The 4K Fire Stick provides Dolby Digital Plus ("DD+") audio to my new Denon A/V receiver on all of the major streaming apps that I use, including those that *don't* support DD+ on the basic Fire Stick such as Disney+ (another good reason to upgrade). But here's the double edge, and it really cuts: If you have a DD+ receiver with a multi-speaker surround setup, and use a live TV streaming app like YouTube TV which supports stereo only, you won't be able to use any of the surround-sound processing modes on your receiver (such as Dolby ProLogic II) because unlike the basic Fire Stick which outputs 2-channel PCM, this one sends a multi-channel signal to the receiver even though only 2 of the channels have any audio. You'll hear the left and right front speakers only; all the other channels will be dead.  The *only* way around this is to set the 4K Fire Stick to "Always Dolby Digital." At that setting, stereo sources will output in stereo as they should and thereby enable ProLogic and other processing modes, but DD+ from streaming apps that support it will be downgraded to Dolby Digital ("DD"), sacrificing the higher bitrate and resolution of DD+. In other words, you can either (1) give up surround sound processing for live TV streaming and settle for 2-channel stereo; (2) give up DD+ on Netflix, Prime, Disney+, &c. and settle for DD; or (3) go to the menu and change the aforementioned setting every time you switch between stereo and multi-channel content, to get the best audio possible from whatever you're about to watch.  Of course, if you don't use an A/V receiver with a multi-speaker surround setup (and/or don't use streaming for live TV or other stereo-only content) this won't affect you; if your receiver and speaker setup is 5.1 and not 7.1 or more, it won't affect you as much and you may not even be able to tell the difference between DD and DD+. (I've never used a sound bar, so I can't speak to those users.) But it seems there's always something with the audio output from these Fire TV devices; as noted above the basic Fire Stick doesn't support DD+ from some apps which the 4K Fire Stick does, but it also doesn't have this problem with stereo sources when set to "Dolby Digital Plus Automatic." Having just recently bought a new receiver to replace a 17-year-old non-HDMI DD/DTS receiver that couldn't decode DD from some apps streaming DD+ and, now, upgraded the basic Fire Stick to this device, I thought my audio problems were over but alas, they're not. Upgrading just meant trading one set of audio glitches/incompatibilities/shortcomings for another, which is quite frustrating.  This has been a known issue for at least two years according to the product forum, so obviously it's never going to be addressed let alone fixed. Again, if you don't use a multi-channel receiver and speaker setup this won't affect you, but if you do, and use a streaming app for live TV, just be wary of this issue before you buy.  UPDATE: There's a separate, related issue with the Netflix app, and how it delivers stereo (non-5.1) content to the receiver from the 4K Fire Stick. No matter what "Surround Sound" is set to, the Netflix app will still send a DD+/DD 5.1 signal to the receiver for stereo content; the sound will come out of the front left and right speakers only and surround-sound processing will be unavailable. Worse yet, if 5.1 content is played after stereo content is played, without exiting Netflix or restarting the device, the 5.1 content will come through in stereo, as described. The only way around *this* is to use a different device, such as a Chromecast or smart-TV app, to watch stereo content on Netflix.  UPDATE 2: Sad to report, although altogether unsurprised, that the new UI update did *not* fix this problem.

There were two reasons we made the jump to Fire TV, cutting the expensive "cable" to satellite or cable tv and the voice command feature.  I'll start with the voice command feature first. We have a blind individual in our household. We needed something simple to use that would get her to content without having a tremendous number of remotes or devices. The firestick fit the bill. It allows her to tune to live tv just by asking Alexa, but she can also access Sirius XM using the same remote. Alexa has excellent voice recognition which makes life much simpler for her. Works beautifully. The remote having just basic functions allows her to easily control volume and power as well - if she doesn't use Alexa directly.  I found that we were streaming more and more television. With our prime membership it allowed us to watch a lot of content for free. I was already enjoying originals like Homecoming and Bosch but with the Fire Stick I could also start getting live tv through Hulu. I have a 4k tv but it is a little older so Hulu live was not directly compatible with my tv. The Fire Stick solved the issue. I have found it fun to be able to ask questions of Alexa like where a city is located if I am unfamiliar. When I'm done, Alexa continues the programming directly where I left off. I leave my tv on the Fire Stick as the default because all my services are available through it. I only go to the other inputs when I want to watch a Blu-ray or play on my Wii-U. Cutting the cord saves me $50 per month - I would imagine that others could save even more.  A great plus is all the apps available. I use OANN, Netflix, Hulu + Live TV, Amazon Prime, Sirius XM, Pandora. There are many others. I can say that I am watching Amazon Prime and Hulu + Live TV much more than Netflix now. Amazon has upped its game with it's new originals.  The remote does work with our Blu-ray but some of the features still need the use of the original remote but that's a minor caveat.  Summing up Firestick TV:  1. Allows viewing of content at a much reduced price 2. Has excellent voice command capabilities 3. Has an excellent selection of apps for various capabilities, including shopping if you want to 4. Has the ability to benefit disabled persons, especially the blind 5. Simple remote that has lots of compatibility 6. 4K ability allows 4K televisions to stream 4K content at no extra cost 7. Setup requires plugging into the power source and a HDMI input. Our tv immediately paired and did not require any further setup. Our Blu-ray was also incredibly easy to setup so no complaints there.  The only con is that some TVs may still need the use of the original remote for some functions - like settings. The same is true of other devices used with the tv.  I highly recommend this device to anyone looking to save money or that has a physical limitation. It works as advertised and actually has surpassed our expectations.

First, I am glad I read the reviews before purchasing. I had recently bought an HDR 4K television, and after purchasing the Fire Stick 4K I found that the video was much softer than my Fire TV pendant had been, almost like it had a shade over it, and was not nearly as sharp and clear as my Fire TV. Then I remembered reading in some of the reviews about the HDR setting, and I found the following in an online article:  If you have an HDR capable television and one of the newer Fire TV models, you probably want to change the Fire TV’s Dynamic Range setting from “Always HDR” to “Adaptive.” This option can be found under the Settings > Display & Sounds > Display menu. Changing this option to adaptive will make it so the Fire TV only switches to HDR when HDR content is played.  This made all the difference! Now the picture is sharp, bright, and very clear.  Secondly, I had a Fire TV Pendant, and a Firestick 2nd gen before that, and BOTH it and my Fire TV Pendant had a VERY annoying random scrolling issue where it would just take off and scroll rapidly in any direction, almost like the remote was stuck, or like you were pressing and holding one of the navigation buttons even though you were not even touching it. I tried putting in fresh batteries, and even had the remote replaced by Amazon, and it still did it with the new remote. It was driving me nuts. I searched online and couldn't find anyone who was having the same issue, so I was at the point where I thought it must be something I was doing, although I am convinced there was a bug in the former devices somewhere. I could sometimes make it happen simply by scrolling down rapidly on the home screen, then it would just take off like a jack rabbit. And it would also happen in any program, like Kodi, and others as well, so I know it was the devices themselves and not an application issue.  So being hopeful that this Firestick 4K might be improved enough to get rid of that issue I took a chance and ordered one. The first thing I noticed is that the battery compartment is different, the batteries are in a single file, instead of side by side. That made me wonder if they had possibly done a total redesign of the remote and the internals, especially considering that it now contains volume controls for the TV. I am happy to report that so far, my luck has held out, and it has not done the rapid scrolling at all (so far). With the Firestick 2nd gen and Fire TV pendant it would happen almost every time I used it, at random times. So far this device has worked perfectly, with no hiccups. And it is VERY snappy, it is at least as fast as the pendant if not a little bit quicker. I am so glad I got this, and so far is the best Fire TV device I have owned to date. I am hoping they are slowly perfecting their products and making them better and better, and I am looking forward to enjoying this device without any scrolling glitches. Thanks Amazon!

I have the fire stick 4k, new in August 2018 - so for two months now. It does most things well, but as many other reviewers have noted, the remote equipment control was only partially implemented and what does work is also intermittent. Amazon's oversights in this regard, and their support stubbornness make the experience very limited.  If you're familiar with CEC equipment control, you know it's supposed to allow any device that supports CEC to receive and send remote control commands over the HDMI cable. In this case, both my fire stick 4K and my Samsung 55" HD TV support CEC and have it enabled.  I guess we could debate which of the following problems are the most serious :-)  1. The first problem is with the fire stick's inability to properly RECEIVE commands over CEC. One of the KEY advantages of CEC is that I should be able to use all the applicable buttons on my Samsung remote to control the fire stick. I know the problem is not with my TV, because when I set the input to my media center, functions work perfectly, including play and pause keys, up/down/right/left arrow keys, FF/REW keys, enter/back/exit keys, etc. But when the TV is set to the fire stick hdmi input, most of those functions don't work, and sometimes what does work stops working until I restart my fire stick. I spent 90 minutes with multiple support folks in chat session - making matters worse, those folks claim that receiving CEC is not supported AT ALL on the fire stick. That's just whacky, it would mean none of my other remotes are usable (eg my TV IR remote, my STB universal IR remote, etc) when using the stick. At least give me play and pause! In reality, what does work in receive mode - sometimes - is the enter key which alternately pauses and plays whatever media is running on the stick. FF and rewind also work, and that is all. As noted, even those functions go away from time to time, requiring restart of the stick.  2. As many reviewers have noted, the TV volume and power controls on the fire stick remote only work in IR mode, when you point the fire remote at the TV. This is a huge miss in my opinion. Since the fire stick remote is bluetooth connected to the stick, there is no reason the stick cannot use CEC so that I don't have to point at the TV. And, as other reviewers noted, scenarios with monitors and other connected equipment become very limited and frustrating.  3. Moving on to the small part of CEC control that support claims is indeed supported, that too is limited and intermittent. When the fire stick settings are correct (correct model TV, control set to automatic, CEC mode, HDMI port of fire stick set, etc) and then when you tell the stick to "play I love lucy", it should power on the TV, set the proper HDMI input port of the TV, and bring up whatever program it thinks you meant by "I love Lucy". Well, it does this - sometimes. And sometimes it does most of it, without powering on the TV, and then when I power on the TV and set the input, I find I love lucy playing. If the TV was already on, it usually changes the input and starts the program properly. Finally, about once per week, all this stops working and I have to restart the fire stick (from settings / my fire stick).  Other: It seems to me one of the reasons for some of the limitations may stem from the simplified (oversimplified?) stick setup for TV control. I only get one working choice for Samsung TV's when running the equipment setup for TV. If, during guided setup of the TV control, I say "No" that power control did not work, it gives me 5 more tries, and none of those actually work, so I'm stuck with the one working Samsung setup, the first one. And I'm not sure that is appropriate for CEC for all of Samsung.  Given the above limitations, an alternative is the fire tv app for android phones and tablets, which seems to be a decent alternative to control the stick playback so at least you don't have to run out and buy extra fire stick remotes for more than one user to have control of a movie. But there's no substitute for using that armchair handheld TV IR remote (or the pile of universals next to it), and that should work, even though they say it should not, and even though it does work, but only partially without play or pause, and even that only works sometimes.  Again all this CEC functionality works perfectly and reliably with my other CEC enabled HDMI connected media players and the same Samsung TV. One of the reasons I dumped my old Roku players was because Roku does not (or didn't used to) support CEC at all. I'm not sure if Roku is considering CEC or not, but I bought the stick because it advertises CEC support. Sad.  For Amazon's abysmal implementation, testing and support of CEC, we can only say "Cmon Man".

The sole reason I bought this item was so that I could actually watch Twitch on my TV without running it through a 3rd party app on my phone and screencasting it to my TV. The bonus is, this Fire Stick also includes every other app you can think of, Amazon Prime, Hulu, Netflix, PlutoTV, Disney+, and the list goes on. It even has browser apps you can download (which my Roku did not have). My biggest question in purchasing this was, would it actually plug into my TV considering these HDMI sticks are so large that they don't fit into some of the ports on the TV, because of the way the TV frame is beveled out. Luckily, this item comes with its own extension cable so that you can plug the cable into your TV and plug the fire stick into the cable. This does not degrade the quality at all.  As far as performance goes, this thing is quick and responsive. Scrolling through menus is ultra fast. Setting up the remote was extremely easy after reading the instructions and going through the on-screen prompts, and now when I hit power on the remote it turns on/off my TV and my sound bar. That's very convenient, considering I was using 3 remotes before (Roku remote, TV remote, sound bar remote). The remote doesn't have an option to change the input on my tv, so I still need the TV remote for that, but that's on rare occasions when I need to flip it over to the DVD player or my Nintendo Switch. The Fire Stick has its own built in sound boost which I had to go in and turn off, because I found while it was boosting sound to make it feel louder and give it more bass, it was muffling the dialogue so much, I had trouble hearing what people were saying. This is probably due to my TaoTronics sound bar as it's not anything worthy of top notch quality sound.  My only beef with this device is that sometimes when I power on my TV using the remote, it will say "no input device," and then I have to switch over to another input and then switch back to the Fire Stick using my TV remote and it will work correctly. I'm not sure what causes this, as the Fire Stick is still running and functioning normally - the TV just isn't recognizing it on power up. This happens about once every 10 to 15 power ups so it's not that big an issue, just a small annoyance.  Overall, this product is an excellent source of entertainment as it has almost every app you can think of to watch TV or stream videos. There are occasional times when it goes on sale, so snag one when you see a price drop if you're worried about the cost.

I bought something for $5.99 and it was here the next day. That's nuts. Then you get Alexa. That's another whole world. The Fire stick 4K has the voice remote with Alexa built in. Download the Alexa app into your cell phone and she is always with you. If you get an invitation to Alexa Auto grab it. Now you can be riding down the road and she is always at the ready. Update: Alexa integration with YouTube TV on totally broken. Suddenly it doesn't understand what "YouTube TV" is, and tries to find things on YouTube. All Alexa commands to YouTube TV now end up with displaying the page to download YouTube, so any voice command or other triggers to tune to specific channels on YouTube TV are now totally useless. Whatever 'update' was deployed today needs to be fixed. It's rather silly to have a remote with voice control that doesn't let you do a simple thing like changing channels.  Original review: I recently switched from a different vendor’s streaming device to the Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K. Extremely happy with the easy setup, the streaming quality (no buffering like the previous device), and the Alexa voice integration. Installing applications was very simple, and using voice control to tune to different channels or tv shows is very user friendly and made it very easy to use. The remote comes with voice control, but if you don’t want to reach for the remote, you can use the voice commands on any other Alexa enabled devices too.  The remaining part of this review is specifically for those who are considering additional Fire TV devices. If you’re only going to get one, there’s no need to read the rest.  After I had used the Fire TV device a while I liked it enough to buy another one for a TV in another room. And that's when I discovered some unexpected and strange limitations in the Alexa integration. In the setup of my second Fire TV Stick 4K I gave the my first and second devices different names, and tried to tune my second device to a different tv channel with Alexa voice commands. The channel was changed - but on the first device, not the second device. There was a clue in the 'conversation' with Alexa though - "Did you mean Fire TV?".  It turns out each Alexa device (Echo Plus, Echo Dot, dimmer switches with Alexa built in, or whatever devices you may have) can only control ONE Fire TV device, and only recognize that device as "Fire TV". (See my workaround for this issue for this below). The name I gave the device (you can set this in https://www.amazon.com/mycd) is not recognized by Alexa. Using the name I gave the Fire TV device in an Alexa command, gave me this response: "I couldn't find a group or device named so-and-so". Using "Fire TV" in the command on the Echo device near the second Fire TV was accepted, and the command was executed - but on the first Fire TV Stick 4K device I had installed, not the second.  In order to control the Fire TV device with a specific Echo device I had to go to in my account online and locate the Echo device, deregister the first Fire TV device and register the second one, and then switch to the Alexa app to link the new Fire TV device to my Echo device. I proceeded to install Youtube TV on the new Fire TV Stick 4K. The Echo device didn’t find any TV channels when I tried for instance ‘tune to ABC on Fire TV’. Again I had to deregister and register the new device in my online account, and link the device in the Alexa app again. And I had to move all my apps and channels around again, which doesn’t take long, it’s just a lot of unnecessary clicks.  As mentioned above, one Echo device can be linked to only one Fire TV device, even though the Fire TV devices have distinct names and Alexa should know how to identify which device you want to command. This may be sufficient for most users, but there are some use cases where it’s not. For instance, if you decide to move from one room to the other, you may want to tell the Echo in the first room to tune the Fire TV in the second room to the right channel before you get there. Or leave the first TV on so you can listen while moving to the second TV and turn it off remotely. Or turn off the TV after you left a room because you decide you’re not going back to watch anymore. As long as each Echo is only controlling one Fire TV device, you can’t do this easily by voice control.  What’s my solution to this? Create Alexa routines using voice as the trigger, and the specific Fire TV device as the target for the command. Btw, the Fire TV devices used in Alexa routines are not listed under the “Smart Home” in the Alexa App, but a few lines above under “Fire TV”. I can turn the Fire TVs on to a specific channel (for instance ABC), or turn them off, from any Echo device now. However, adding multiple voice control commands to turn the tv on remotely to specific channels (NBC, CBS etc) seems to confuse Alexa: Only the first routine works across Echo devices, additional routines seem to be device specific again.  Whether you really need to create a bunch of routines to use voice commands to control your Fire TV devices from other rooms is entirely up to you. I would like the voice commands for my devices’ Alexa integration to be for specific actions and available with any Alexa device, and not be limited by location because the Alexa device closest to me can only control a specific Fire TV device.  Lots of extra work, and given that the devices have distinct names in the Alexa app this workaround shouldn’t be necessary. Disappointed that the integration is so tricky, plenty of room for improvement there, so removing one star.

I picked up this streaming stick yesterday at Best Buy to replace my old First Generation Fire TV box. Needless to say this stick is a huge upgrade in software and usability over my old box. Faster response times in all apps and the new remote alone makes it worth upgrading.  Once I hooked the stick up it went through an easy setup process to recognize my TV and also find how to operate my old Yamaha Digital Sound Projector to control volume and mute functions. The power button on the remote controls my TV off and on as well. This effectively eliminates the need for my receiver and TV remote for most things. This is why I said the remote alone makes it worth the purchase. If you already have a device that is compatible with the new remote you can buy it separately for $30. I should note that my 1st Gen Fire TV does not work with the new remote and would not pair with it as it is not compatible.  Beyond the remote and visual updates for 4K TVs, everything else is the same from a software perspective. This means if you are a Prime or Prime Video subscriber you will find a lot of benefits from the way content is presented. It definitely favors more to the Amazon Prime members. What is less focused to Amazon is when you do voice searches where content will be favored to watch for free from apps installed. As an example, when I did a search for the movie Rocky I saw the first choice to watch is for free on my Sony Crackle app. This is in spite of the fact that you could also purchase or rent the movie from Amazon. What is great about this search is the number of apps that are included in the search. This is better then the Apple TV but less then the Roku searches on their devices. Yes, you will find more apps on Roku searches which could lead to opportunities to watch content for free or at a reduced price on multiple services. The visual appearance and voice search on the Fire TV however are far superior to Roku and this does not even include the extra functions built-in with Alexa. What got me into the Fire TV years ago was the voice search and it is still great today but not as advanced as Apple TV's Siri voice search.  At this time I would put the Fire TV as the second best streaming box I have used. The Apple TV is still the best, but the gap is narrowing. Where the Apple TV exceeds is the outstanding advanced voice search functions with Siri and the TV App which pushes more diversity in content sources. However the Apple TV is expensive and if you are not an Apple person it is hard to beat the price and features of Fire TV in any form. This 4K stick is a great value for the price and features which is why I am giving it 5 stars.

After struggling with Tablo DVR connectivity and poor-to-no performance issues for 3 months, I finally decided to try the Amazon Fire TV and TV recast system. It works Great!!! I originally went with Tablo to avoid extra hardware (ie. a fire stick at each TV) and trusting many “best of” reviews available out on the web, but at the low price of a few fire sticks vs. months of 100% frustration and time lost with Tablo never working, it is very worth it to make the switch to the fire TV system. Plus with Fire Recast I don’t have to pay the two subscriptions Tablo requires (one TV Guide and one to even make the Tablo software even remotely useable) ...but both of which are useless when the Tablo won’t even play a live tv stream, nor connect, nor play back a recorded stream, ...). The technical support at Tablo pretends to not understand that their firmware/software has severe issues which randomly cripples the devices operation. They focus instead on telling the customer they have poor reception. Well news flash Tablo: you’re always going to have fringe channels that any channel scan picks up which a device sold for the purpose of HDTV watching and recording which requires the device to be able to effectively deal with. And besides, the fringe channels weren’t even being watched or recorded so it is an even bigger firmware problem if fringe channels are causing a Tablo to lock up all the time.  Amazon has the technology down! Fringe channels are almost nonexistent since switching over to Fire recast. Likely due to better antenna signal sensitivity and digital signal processing algorithms.  Also haven’t had a single major issue with the Fire TV system for what’s going on a month now. Sometimes the image is a little fuzzy, but then shortly after it clears up. I assume this is due to the device adjusting to WiFi network conditions and both network and recast optimizing when they can. But it’s better than a device (like Tablo) that locks up and becomes unresponsive to where you can’t even change a channel or connect for that matter. The Tablo would always negotiate the WiFi connection rate (throughput as measured by my upgrade router) down to the lowest rate it could (6 Mbps in my case) and just get stuck there indefinitely or sometimes would reset the following day. At 6Mbps the Tablo would not stream anything and often even fail to connect. I upgraded my entire WiFi network trying to get Tablo to work, but everything else works incredibly great on both my old and new WiFi networks (ie. Fire cast/fire stick, stream Netflix, Amazon Prime, etc.) all over WiFi without any issues. It was also random if a power cycle was going to restore Tablo to a better WiFi throughput rate or not.

My cable TV bill bundle (TV, Internet and Phone) was over $228 a month!! I just could not justify paying that much for something we didn't use enough. So I looked for various things to take it's place.  Well after researching quite a bit (over 4 months worth) I chose this Fire TV. I am so glad I did! We cut Cable TV and Cable Phone, we use Cell strictly now, (and no 911 is not an issue, you can call them and register the number for the address where you live, takes 5 minutes). So now all we have is cable internet, and it's less than half the cost.  The Fire TV allows you to hook it up to your wired or wireless internet and stream media over it. You download "Apps" just like you use on your phone to it and play videos, movies, and music through it onto your TV.  I wanted to make sure I could get local channels (Over the air was not an option because of where I live) so I looked at different apps. I settled on Playstaton Vue (no you don't have to own a PlayStation to use it). It is a TV streaming service that gives you choices of what you want to pay for (tiers) and also gives you local channels. It detects where you live by the internet signal and feeds local TV onto the list of channels you pick. IT's FAR cheaper than cable TV and quite frankly just as easy to use. Has a guide like a cable TV and even a DVR system to allow you to record shows to watch later, this is all on PlayStation Vue.  Add apps (free) like YouTube, Netflix, Hulu and any others you can think of including the free ones (there is a way to jailbreak the FireTV and allow downloading of almost any app to it if you want) and you have a huge selection of TV and Movies to choose from. I now have one on each of the three TV's in the house. My son loves it on the TV in his room.  All told with paying for Cable Internet and the streaming services I have (PlayStation Vue and NetFlix) I am paying around $110. That's less than half what I was paying.  One thing to consider is what "level" of internet access you have. I already had raised my internet level of service (number of GIG's a month and speed) because I ran a lot of devices and internet stuff so I didn't have to up that, but you may want to see how much data you will use in a month and may need to up your internet level with your provider.  Overall it's great and easy to install and use. Uses one of the HDMI ports on your TV. And it will even turn your TV on and off. Does require it's own electric plug for the power source.
